'''''Oenothera rosea''''', also known as '''rosy evening-primrose''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''rose evening primrose''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=OERO|taxon=Oenothera rosea|accessdate=21 July 2015}}</ref> '''pink evening primrose''', or '''Rose of Mexico''', is a species of flowering plant in the family Onagraceae. It is native to the Americas but can also be found as an introduced species in several regions of the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oenothera rosea L'Hér. ex Aiton {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:173348-2 |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>  It can spread quickly across yards and fields, and removal takes years of sustained effort.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bender |first=Steve |date=1 March 2025 |title=Why You Shouldn't Plant Pink Evening Primrose In Your Yard |url=https://www.southernliving.com/pink-evening-primrose-6534732 |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=[[Southern Living]] |language=en}}</ref>

''Oenothera rosea'' has flowers with less than {{convert|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} diameter. The shade varies from pink to red.<ref name="Botanica 612">"Botanica. The Illustrated AZ of over 10000 garden plants and how to cultivate them", p. 612. Könemann, 2004. {{ISBN|3-8331-1253-0}}</ref>
